shifts.title: AI agents get a line manager
announced: Shows what is driving AI spend, sets spending policies and sends alerts.
Tracks agent success rate, user satisfaction and hours of work assisted.
Agent usage insights in the Microsoft 365 admin center
Available without an Agent 365 licence for Microsoft-built agents.
shifts.why: Microsoft's own launch materials cite McKinsey research: 93% of organisations have gone over their AI budgets, and AI spending can nearly quadruple once it scales company-wide. Agents are now being managed like a cost centre, with budgets, alerts and performance reviews.
shifts.monday: Name one owner for AI spend. Agree on two measures, such as hours assisted and task success rate, before you scale any agent past a pilot.

shifts.title: Copilot becomes where the workday starts
announced: Create and edit documents from inside Copilot.
A start page that recommends what to work on.
A daily briefing in Outlook and the Copilot app.
Personal agents that keep working on long tasks.
shifts.why: Microsoft wants Copilot, not Word or Outlook, to be the first screen people open. Census data shows 27% of US businesses already have staff using generative AI for work, so habits are forming now in whichever tool is open first.
shifts.monday: Pick three routine workflows (the weekly report, meeting prep, first drafts of proposals). Run them through Copilot with one team for a month and measure the time saved.

shifts.title: You'll pay for usage, not just seats
announced: Windows 365 for Agents can now be paid for with Copilot Credits.
Requires Copilot Credits. Today Brief is included with a Copilot licence.
Forecasting and optimisation for AI spend.
shifts.why: More features are now billed by usage on top of per-person licences. AI costs start to behave like cloud bills: they vary month to month and grow with adoption. Most budgets aren't built for that yet.
shifts.monday: Ask finance to model AI as a consumption cost, the same way you budget for cloud, with a monthly cap and an alert threshold.

shifts.title: Copilot works with tools beyond Microsoft
announced: More than 38 prebuilt sales skills inside Copilot.
Pulls business context from more than 350 third-party connectors.
Fabric IQ connectors for ChatGPT and Claude
Your Fabric data can be used in other companies' AI assistants.
shifts.why: Most businesses run a mix of vendors, such as Salesforce for CRM, SAP for ERP and Google for some teams. Copilot now connects to tools outside Microsoft, so you don't need an all-Microsoft setup to get value from it.
shifts.monday: List where your most important data lives (CRM, ERP, shared drives). Check which of those systems already connect to Copilot before you buy another standalone AI tool.

shifts.title: Security teams now have to govern agents as well as people
announced: Gives each AI agent its own identity with access policies, as people have.
Stops Copilot from using sensitive files, even ones nobody has labelled.
Monitors or blocks AI agents running on Windows PCs.
Security agents that work together. Its triage agent handles about 80% of the alerts in a typical Defender queue.
shifts.why: Every agent can read files, send messages and act on its own. Microsoft is now building identity, access and threat-protection tools aimed at agents, so governing them belongs on the security team's job list.
shifts.monday: Make a list of every AI agent and assistant in use, including unofficial ones. Record who owns it, what it can access and what it can do.
